svg.title: Suspected meningitis or encephalitis: blood culture and empiric treatment first, CT before the lumbar puncture only with focal signs or a decreased level of consciousness, then the CSF, read against normal values, separates bacterial meningitis, aseptic (viral) meningitis and herpes simplex encephalitis, each with its organisms and treatment; bacterial meningitis ends with its complications

svg.text: Fever · headache · stiff neck · altered mental status: think MENINGITIS

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: classic triad: FEVER, ALTERED MENTAL STATUS, NUCHAL RIGIDITY (Kernig's, Brudzinski's)

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: language trouble, confusion, focal seizures → think ENCEPHALITIS (the brain itself)

svg.text: 4 kinds of CNS infection: bacterial (meningitis, abscess) · viral (meningitis, encephalitis) · fungal (cryptococcal) · protozoal

svg.text: 2 · START EMPIRIC treatment now: never wait for the CT or the tap

svg.text: 3 · CT/MRI FIRST only if focal signs or ↓ consciousness (PUNISH: Papilledema, Unconscious, Neurologic deficit, Immunocompromised, Seizure,

svg.text: History of CNS disease) · also poorly seen fundi, from a NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS area → mass = NEUROSURGERY
